correctness.rationale: For rank-two A=BB^T, diagonal pivot mass p_i=||b_i||²/T and relative second-coordinate power t_i produce R_i=λ2+(λ1−λ2)t_i, while sum p_it_i=λ2/T. The explicit symmetric signed Gram-row pairs realize any finite law of that prescribed mean with exactly eigenvalues (λ1,λ2). Jensen, chord convexity and a one-sided two-atom extremizer imply every stated tight variance and tail bound. Exact fractions verify three spectrum-preserving examples and 1,116 independent full-rank integer-Gram tests; 100 three-atom tests supplement the infinite-quantifier constructive proof. Cases u=m,u=λ1,u>λ1 and zero-diagonal pivots are covered.

originality.rationale: The ordinary diagonal-proportional pivot and expected residual matrix are prior (arXiv:2207.06503); neither that identity nor multistep high-probability bounds (arXiv:2608.20633), broader pivot convergence (arXiv:2609.06287), or alternate pivot distributions (arXiv:2404.11487) entail the exact converse that every finite mean-constrained rank-two one-step trace law is realizable at fixed spectrum. Targeted literature and published-finding corpus searches plus accessible historical claim comparisons found no equal or stronger implication. Historical priority remains uncertain against unindexed frame constructions.
residual_risks: An equivalent abstract two-dimensional frame or prescribed random-Rayleigh quotient law may exist in unindexed literature.
The converse construction requires freedom to increase ambient dimension; fixing a small dimension changes the attainable class.
Only primary sections indicated above were materially compared; comprehensive global priority is not certified.

value.rationale: A natural and complete finite-dimensional classification of uncertainty for a widely used randomized numerical factorization at fixed rank-two spectrum. It determines exactly which distributional guarantees can be inferred from eigenvalues alone, rather than from just the already-known mean: each convex risk extremum, minimal and maximal variance, and all optimal threshold probabilities, including explicit four-row tail extremizers. The statistic is the actual post-pivot trace residual, directly used to evaluate kernel approximation quality. Generalization to higher rank and fixed dimension remains open.
